claims.claim: The personal-import VAT/purchase-tax exemption ceiling has changed three times in six months: raised from USD 75 to USD 150 by ministerial order in December 2025, revoked by the Knesset on 24 February 2026, and reset to USD 130 by a fresh Finance Ministry order effective midnight 24-25 February 2026. As of May 2026 the current threshold is USD 130.
claims.source_title: Defying Knesset, Smotrich ups tax exemption for online purchases from abroad to $130 - Times of Israel

additional_sources.title: Knesset revokes measure that made more online purchases tax-exempt - Times of Israel (24 February 2026)
Minister of Finance Expands Tax Exemption on Personal Imports - gov.il press release 26 November 2025 (initial USD 150 announcement, since superseded)

claims.raw_snippet: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich initially raised the personal-import VAT/purchase-tax exemption ceiling from USD 75 to USD 150 via ministerial order announced 26 November 2025 (effective December 2025). The Knesset revoked that order on 24 February 2026. The same day, Smotrich signed a fresh order setting the threshold at USD 130, effective at midnight between 24-25 February 2026. As of May 2026 the operative ceiling is USD 130.
